title: Perseus: The Gorgon's Head
subtitle: A mirrored shield, a sleeping monster, and a winged horse

learningObjectives.text: How does Perseus kill Medusa without being turned to stone?
What is born from her death?

main.author: Pseudo-Apollodorus
main.note: Verbatim passage from the named work/translation; the locator selects this exact local source segment.
main.excerpt: So Perseus stood over them as they slept, and while Athena guided his hand and he looked with averted gaze on a brazen shield, in which he beheld the image of the Gorgon

narrativeBlocks.title: Three sisters, one mortal
narrativeBlocks.body: There are three Gorgons — and only Medusa can die. All three have snakes for hair and a gaze that turns the beholder to stone; approaching any of them awake is suicide.

narrativeBlocks.title: The mirrored shield
narrativeBlocks.body: Perseus finds them asleep and does not look at them. He watches only the reflection in Athena's polished shield, hovering overhead while the goddess steadies his sword-arm — the story's defining image: never look directly at the thing that destroys you.

narrativeBlocks.title: One stroke, two births
narrativeBlocks.body: The blade falls and Medusa's head comes off — and from her neck spring two children of Poseidon: the winged horse Pegasus and the warrior Chrysaor. Even monsters' deaths generate new myth.

narrativeBlocks.title: Escape by invisibility
narrativeBlocks.body: The immortal sisters wake screaming to pursue. Perseus is already gone — the cap of invisibility, the winged sandals, and the head sealed in the knapsack. The trophy that killed no one looks exactly like a severed head in a bag.

narrativeBlocks.title: The trickster's kill
narrativeBlocks.body: Unlike Heracles' bare-handed wrestling, Perseus wins by equipment and indirection — the reflection, the cap, the bag. Different heroes, different technologies of victory.

quiz.prompt: How does Perseus behead Medusa safely?

choices.text: He wears a blindfold and strikes by sound
He turns her to stone with her own gaze
He approaches while the Gorgons sleep and watches only her reflection in Athena's mirrored shield as he strikes
He sends Pegasus to attack first

quiz.explanation: Direct sight is fatal; the shield's reflection is the entire trick.

quiz.prompt: What is born when Medusa dies?

choices.text: Pegasus the winged horse and the warrior Chrysaor — her children by Poseidon, springing from her severed neck

quiz.explanation: Greek myth recycles everything — the monster's death generates the hero's mount and another line of giants.
